version   r160 (npm: three@0.160.0)

source    https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.min.js
size      669884 bytes

vendored  2026-08-06

Why this exact build
--------------------
`scripts/export_model_3d.py` inlines this file into
`structured/candidates/model3d.html` so the viewer is a single file that opens
by double-clicking, with no web server and no network.

That rules out the ES-module builds (`build/three.module.js`): Chrome blocks
module scripts loaded over `file://` as a cross-origin request, so a module
build would leave the viewer blank for exactly the audience it is meant for
(family members opening the file from a shared folder).

r160 is the last release that still publishes `build/three.min.js`; r170 and
later return 404 for that path. Loading it prints one deprecation warning to
the console — that line is expected, not a fault.

OrbitControls is deliberately NOT vendored: it ships only as an ES module under
`examples/jsm/`, which has the same `file://` problem. The viewer hand-rolls
orbit/pan/zoom instead.

Upgrading
---------
Any newer three.js means giving up the single-file `file://` guarantee. If that
guarantee is ever dropped, switch to the module build plus an import map and
serve the viewer over HTTP; otherwise stay on r160.
